summary.headline: Aditya Infotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 89.9% YoY to ₹1,746 crore, and FY27 revenue guidance was raised to ₹6,500–6,800 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,746 crore (+89.9% YoY, +24.5% QoQ) with EBITDA of ₹307 crore at a 17.6% margin, up from 14.8% in Q1. Reported PAT was ₹185.5 crore after a ₹34.4 crore exceptional fire loss at the Kadapa plant, which is insured; PAT before exceptional was ₹220 crore. Management raised FY27 revenue and PAT margin guidance but kept the EBITDA margin at 14–15%, citing expected lower second-half margins from input cost pressure in SOC and memory. The company completed a ₹1,500 crore QIP in September and became debt-free in October.

segments.name: CP Plus (core brand)
segments.commentary: About 88% of Q2 revenue vs 86% a year ago; IP products are about 79% of CP Plus, up from 71%. Company share of total Indian video surveillance market (incl. unorganised) was about 42% in the 12 months to Sep 2026, up from 30% at IPO.

segments.name: Nextiveo and Ira brands
segments.commentary: Nextiveo targets entry-level and Ira targets mid-market. Nextiveo's pickup is described as good; Ira's first products are expected to reach market by end-December 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue raised to ₹6,500–6,800 crore from ₹6,000–6,500 crore, implying 54–61% growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin kept at 14–15% despite 16.3% in H1, to keep a cushion for market share strategy and input cost volatility.
FY27 PAT margin raised to 9–10% from 8.5–9.5%.
Second-half margins expected to be below Q2 as low-cost SOC and memory inventory is used up and price increases are passed on gradually.
FY27 market share guided to 43–45%, up from the earlier view.
Backward integration benefits (housing, cable JV) expected mainly from FY28; not modelled into guidance yet.
Medium term: unit market growth of 18–20% over 3–5 years; value growth expected to exceed unit growth in the near term as prices still rise.
capex_capacity: Kadapa plant capacity is 2.5 million units per month; Kadapa phase 3 (22 acres newly acquired) and a new Greater Noida facility, funded from the QIP, aim to double capacity by FY29-early FY30.
Total capex planned at about ₹650 crore for the capacity doubling; Greater Noida civil construction starts next quarter, with capacity online in about 18–24 months.
Housing and enclosures plant in Kadapa begins trials this quarter, with commercial production next quarter; cable plant goes live in Q4 FY27.
Planned fully integrated lens plant in Greater Noida with capacity of 2 million lenses per month.
Blue K-Graph AI investment: ₹45.4 crore for 30% fully diluted stake, with one board seat and one observer seat; completion subject to customary conditions.
demand_pricing: Price increases on SOC, DDR and memory are being passed to channel gradually to protect market share and avoid a channel price shock; the company took strategic inventory positions ahead of cost increases.
About 40+ brands are STQC-certified per the online portal; management sees no significant on-ground entry traction yet.
Government policy on DVR/NVR is still a work in progress; no new notification issued as yet.

Channel reach: 30–35 thousand installers/resellers on the app and about 2,000 system integrators; management cites about 350,000 outlets in the addressable market, with the market leader present at 278,000.
Management said H1 growth of about 90% was partly helped by a soft base when STQC certification backlogs held back industry supply last year; H2 growth expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 14–15% full-year margin guide, what do back-calculated H2 margins (~13%) imply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said backward integration benefits will mainly flow in FY28, and kept the 14–15% guide as a prudent cushion given volatile SOC and memory costs, as the company has historically over-delivered.

qa_highlights.question: What capabilities beyond Blue are being sought in inorganic moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a 'CP Plus 2.0' plan to move from hardware to solutions, cloud and AI with a global footprint. Targets are capabilities (AI, cloud, storage IP), product adjacencies and geographic expansion; specific targets were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is pricing being passed on gradually, and is there demand pushback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is staggering price increases to protect competitive position and grow share, aiming above the 43–45% share guide.

qa_highlights.question: Is Blue a meaningful revenue contributor over 3–5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blue is mainly a technology and capability play, bringing cloud storage and analytics attach to cameras, not a standalone large revenue driver.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export plan and its timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export entry is planned within 18–24 months, focused on China-plus-one markets, with product mix (Pro or entry) varying by market; entry mode (own brand, partnership or OEM) is still being decided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth and margin outlook beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 18–20% unit growth over 3–5 years; value growth should exceed unit growth near term as prices rise. Backward integration margin benefits are not yet modelled.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables improve and does it hold across brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tighter collection is a conscious effort and efficiency gain, and it expects similar receivable levels across Ira, Nextiveo and CP Plus Pro on a blended basis.

risks_watch: Input cost volatility in SOC, DDR and memory; the timing of price pass-through and the margin path in H2 FY27.
Working capital is elevated due to strategic inventory buys; receivable and inventory normalisation should be tracked.
Pending government policy on DVR/NVR certification could change domestic brand competition.
Ira brand launch (December 2026) and CP Plus Pro rollout (Q4 FY27) execution.
Capex execution: Greater Noida and Kadapa phase 3 (₹650 crore) timelines, and backward integration plants (housing, cables, lenses).
Full benefit of debt-free balance sheet and lower finance cost from H2 FY27.
Insurance claim on the Kadapa fire (₹34.4 crore exceptional item) settlement.
Blue K-Graph integration and the still-undisclosed CP Plus 2.0 acquisition pipeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, share gains and the raised revenue and PAT guidance, but deliberately conservative on margins, with the EBITDA guide held at 14–15%. Management was evasive on specific M&A targets, the H1 growth split, and the housing plant spend, and deferred on backward integration benefits.
key_quotes: This has been the strongest half in our history.
Q2 should not be read as the run rate.
We want to be prudent and as our history is we have always over delivered from our guidance and we would want to maintain the cushion in order to ensure and go for market share as well.
The blue acquisition for us is more of a tech learning and less of a revenue or a bit of credit from an approach perspective.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to ₹6,500–6,800 crore (54–61% growth), backed partly by demand/share gains (FY27 share guide 43–45%) and price pass-through, while the ~₹650 crore capacity doubling (Kadapa phase 3, Greater Noida) only comes online in 18–24 months, so near-term growth is largely not capacity-backed; management also flagged H2 normalisation off a soft base.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA guide held at 14-15% versus 16.3% in H1, with management flagging H2 margins below Q2's 17.6% as low-cost SOC and memory inventory runs out and price rises pass through gradually; backward-integration benefits deferred to FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cable plant goes live in Q4 FY27 and Kadapa housing plant reaches commercial production next quarter, but the ~650 crore capacity doubling only comes online in 18-24 months (FY29-early FY30), so near-term growth is largely not capacity-backed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guide raised to 6,500-6,800 crore (54-61% growth) and share guided to 43-45%, though management flagged H2 normalising from a soft STQC-backlog base that flattered H1 growth of about 90%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Greater Noida civil works next quarter
rows.why: About 650 crore capacity-doubling capex is already approved and funded from the 1,500 crore QIP, with Greater Noida civil construction starting next quarter; a further lens plant (2 million lenses/month) is planned but undated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue and PAT margin guidance were already raised this quarter, and management says it historically over-delivers on the held 14-15% EBITDA margin cushion, but H2 growth is expected to normalise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input cost pressure in SOC and memory and gradual price pass-through could compress H2 margins, and H2 growth normalises off a soft base, though the 14-15% EBITDA guide already embeds a cushion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Ira by end-Dec 2026; CP Plus Pro in Q4 FY27
rows.why: Ira's first products are expected to reach market by end-December 2026 and the CP Plus Pro rollout is scheduled for Q4 FY27; Nextiveo pickup is described as good.

rows.label: Export entry in China-plus-one markets
rows.why: Management plans export entry within 18-24 months, but entry mode (own brand, partnership or OEM) is still undecided, so no revenue is yet committed.

rows.label: Blue K-Graph AI stake (30%) and CP Plus 2.0 M&A
rows.why: The 45.4 crore for 30% of Blue K-Graph is subject to customary conditions and is mainly a capability play; CP Plus 2.0 targets are undisclosed, so this is an uncertain trigger rather than a committed one.

rows.label: DVR/NVR certification policy
rows.why: Government DVR/NVR policy is still a work in progress with no notification yet, and STQC-certified entrants (40+ brands) show no significant on-ground traction so far.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains and the raised revenue and PAT guidance but deliberately conservative on the 14-15% EBITDA margin; it was evasive on M&A targets, H1 growth split and housing plant spend, with analysts probing on the H2 margin implied at about 13%.
